identity.title: Legal Practicum
identity.byline: John O. Sonsteng · Damien A. Riehl · Roger S. Haydock

hero.eyebrow: A LIVING CASEBOOK · 50 YEARS OF METHOD
hero.heading: The Legal practice practicum: a working law firm for law students
hero.lede: A brief introduction:The day law students. Graduate from law school they should be practice ready.Although Law professors are excellent teachers, scholars, published authors, responsible for governance of the law school and active contributors to the community.  The demands and expectations placed on law professors can be, at times, overwhelming. With the time available law schools are very effective and providing focusedtraining to students. Law schools are a effective source of training in the following areas: ……..  Because of the limitation of time and resources, there are many areas in which the law school is not the primary educator. The primary source of training in the following areas is the lawyers own experience..  The legal practice practicums provide legal practice education in most of the areas where training is now  based only on the lawyer’s experience.  The legal practice practicums provide this training through the law schools without sacrificing any areas in which the law schools are so successful, without diminishing students’ other legal education and without additional cost. The LEGAL PRACTICE PRACTICUMS address matters across different legal practice areas and two jurisdiction tiers, a surveyed skills taxonomy mapped to FOLIO, simulated client interviews, and the complete business of a two-lawyer firm — every page generated from one open data spine.

M1.title: Foundational
M1.thesis: The groundwork — how to think, read, and carry yourself as a lawyer before the substance arrives.

M2.title: Substantive + Skills
M2.thesis: The trades of lawyering, learned on real-shaped matters across ten practice areas.

M3.title: Transition to Practice
M3.thesis: The business of law and the professional judgment that turns a graduate into a practitioner.

sample.title: Watch a sample consultation ▸
sample.description:
A recorded client interview — Devon Halvard, charged with DWI —
      played back turn by turn, then assessed with feedback. See the consultation room and the debrief in action
      before you bring your own key. Scripted sample, not a live AI client.

matters.description:
Ten practice shapes, each in the fictional State of Meridian
      and again in a real jurisdiction. Full packets, case files, rubrics, and interviews.

firm.title: Firm dashboard
firm.description:
Ellingboe & Ravndal LLP — the two-lawyer practicum firm.
      Fees, realization, AR aging, trust accounting, and budget, charted and taught.

templates.title: Deliverable templates
templates.description:
The six recurring course handouts — time sheet, engagement
      letter, interview plan, settlement plan, portfolio, and reflective report — each presented as a
      Planning Guide and Checklist with assessment and feedback notes. Print-ready.

centaur.title: People first; technology as the tool
centaur.description: Every exercise here ships with a machine-readable rubric and a revise-and-repeat loop. Faculty coach students through live work with people. Technology supplies more practice repetitions under faculty supervision. Technology gives the first-pass assessment and feedback, at any hour. The simulated client interviews, rubric feedback, and firm dashboard below support that practice.

getting_started.title: Getting started at your school
getting_started.description: Meet the people who run the practicum, shape it around your school, and find free matters and templates to begin.
